title: Using Inspectors `Save (as)` on `VoxelGIData` prompts it to be saved as `.tres` or `.tscn` rather than `.res`
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible: 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon R7 Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.20913.2000) - AMD A12-9720P RADEON R7, 12 COMPUTE CORES 4C+8G (4 threads) - 7.46 GiB memory - WASAPI (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The default way to store `VoxelGIData` files is in `.res` rather than `.tres` files, so much so, that Godot gives a popup message on every save when the data is saved as a `.tres` instead. When using the `Bake VoxelGI` button on a `VoxelGI` node, the default extension it gives for storing the data is a `.res` file. When instead using the Inspector and using the `Save As` context menu (or the Save button if the data was made unique), it gives a default extension of `.tres`. It also has been giving me an issue where it attempts to save it as a `.tscn`, with the default name being that of a different (unrelated) scene, which was previously saved using the `Save As` context on the scene tab. Using the `Save As` context on the VoxelGIData then attempts to save it under the same name and extension. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add a VoxelGI node. 2. Bake the VoxelGI node, and store the data as a .res file. 3. Open the VoxelGI node in the inspector 4. Right-click the data 5. Save As OR Make Unique > Save 6. The suggested extension for the VoxelGIData is now .tres If you open a different scene, and Save As the scene under a different name and leave it opened before going through these steps (and use Save As to store the VoxelGIData), you will likely get the issue where it attempts to save it as a .tscn instead. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
